body.text: Brief requirements (from the supervisor's messages of 19 November 2026, answering the agent's review of the manuscript 'Half Central Moment for Data Analysis'): (1) the claimset is to be prepared from a lab study, and the paper then submitted to JASA or another statistics journal; (2) values above the mean are the real part of the HCM, as equation (5) has it; the prose is to say so; (3) fix the proof of Theorem 1; (4) explain what the Asymmetry coefficient measures; (5) find a bounded version of the Complex Extremity; (6) make the experiments rigorous and correct; (7) find papers that use half moments or something similar; (8) compare the coefficients with existing measures, with references; (9) study robustness by simulation; (10) establish sampling properties of the estimators; (11) give the sharp sample bound of Hypotailedness; (12) keep the sign convention of Asymmetry (positive when the real part, above the mean, is larger), because swapping parts or angle breaks the construction; (13) give the coefficients for more distributions. References: the manuscript's library.bib, supplied by the supervisor.

Work done before this record began: on 19 November 2026, before the study was set up, the agent checked the manuscript in scratch work outside any record (numerical integration of the closed forms, exact values behind the figure captions, a search for a counterexample to the converse of Theorem 1, a numerical minimisation of the sample Hypotailedness, coefficients of further distributions, and a reproduction of Table 1 from R's rock data with greybox). Those checks informed the agent's review and the hypotheses it will propose. They are re-run here as exploratory runs so that every number comes from a recorded run; a hypothesis they suggested is recorded as coming from exploration.

body.text: Which properties do the half central moment and the coefficients built on it (Asymmetry, Hypotailedness, Extremity, Complex Extremity) have: their bounds and when the bounds are reached, their behaviour under symmetry and under changes of location and scale, what Asymmetry measures, how small Hypotailedness can be in a sample, and how a single outlying value affects them in the population (their influence functions)?
What are the half central moment and its coefficients, in closed form, for standard parametric distributions, and for which of them is there no closed form?

How do the half-moment coefficients of a sample respond to one value moved further and further from the centre, compared with moment, L-moment, quantile and mean-based measures of skewness and tail weight?
What do the half-moment coefficients show on real data (the petroleum rock samples and the daily returns of four European stock indices), next to the competing measures of skewness and tail weight?

body.definition: The half central moment (HCM) of a variable $y$ with finite mean $\mu_1$: $\mu_{0.5} = \mathrm{E}\left[(y - \mu_1)^{0.5}\right]$, the square root taken as the principal root, so that $\mu_{0.5} = \mathrm{E}\left[(y-\mu_1)_+^{0.5}\right] + i\,\mathrm{E}\left[(\mu_1-y)_+^{0.5}\right]$: the real part $\mathcal{R}$ comes from the values above the mean and the imaginary part $\mathcal{I}$ from those below it. Sample estimate: $m_{0.5} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} (y_j - m_1)^{0.5}$, with $m_1$ the sample mean.
The half absolute moment (HAM): $\nu_{0.5} = \mathcal{R}(\mu_{0.5}) + \mathcal{I}(\mu_{0.5}) = \mathrm{E}|y - \mu_1|^{0.5}$; sample estimate $v_{0.5} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} |y_j - m_1|^{0.5}$.

Asymmetry $= 1 - \phi/(\pi/4) = \frac{4}{\pi}\arctan\left(\frac{\mathcal{R}(\mu_{0.5}) - \mathcal{I}(\mu_{0.5})}{\nu_{0.5}}\right)$, where $\phi = \mathrm{Arg}(\mu_{0.5}) \in [0, \pi/2]$; positive when the part above the mean is the larger. The sample coefficient uses $m_{0.5}$ and $v_{0.5}$.
Hypotailedness $= \nu_{0.5}/\sigma^{0.5}$ for a variable with finite positive variance $\sigma^2$; the sample coefficient divides $v_{0.5}$ by $\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j}(y_j - m_1)^2\right)^{0.25}$.
Extremity $= 2\,\mathrm{Hypotailedness}^{p} - 1$ with $p = \log 0.5 / \log(2 \times 3^{-0.75}) \approx 5.30$, so that the uniform distribution has Extremity 0.
CH $= \mu_{0.5}/\sigma^{0.5}$, the half central moment divided by the square root of the standard deviation (the manuscript of 19 November 2026).

For a variable with finite variance and deviation $D = y - \mu_1$: $H_+ = \mathrm{E}\left[D^{0.5} \mid D > 0\right] / \left(\mathrm{E}\left[D^2 \mid D > 0\right]\right)^{0.25}$ above the mean and $H_- = \mathrm{E}\left[|D|^{0.5} \mid D < 0\right] / \left(\mathrm{E}\left[D^2 \mid D < 0\right]\right)^{0.25}$ below it; in a sample, the same ratios over the values above and below the sample mean.

The bounded Complex Extremity proposed in this study: $\mathrm{CE} = \left(2H_+^{p} - 1\right) + i\left(2H_-^{p} - 1\right)$, with $H_\pm$ the one-sided Hypotailedness and $p = \log 0.5 / \log(2 \times 3^{-0.75})$; the real part describes the values above the mean.
The standardised third central moment $\mathrm{E}[(y-\mu_1)^3]/\sigma^3$; sample version with $1/n$ moments.
The standardised fourth central moment minus 3, $\mathrm{E}[(y-\mu_1)^4]/\sigma^4 - 3$; sample version with $1/n$ moments.
The L-moment ratio $\tau_3 = \lambda_3/\lambda_2$; sample version from unbiased probability-weighted moments.
The L-moment ratio $\tau_4 = \lambda_4/\lambda_2$; sample version from unbiased probability-weighted moments.
The trimmed L-moment ratio $\tau_3^{(1)}$ with trimming (1,1), which exists without moments.
The trimmed L-moment ratio $\tau_4^{(1)}$ with trimming (1,1).
Bowley-Hinkley quartile skewness $(Q_3 + Q_1 - 2Q_2)/(Q_3 - Q_1)$; sample quartiles by R type 7.
The medcouple, a robust skewness measure in $[-1, 1]$ built from the median of a kernel over pairs of values on either side of the median.

Skewness centred at the mean, $2F(\mu_1) - 1$ ($F$ the distribution function), bounded in $[-1, 1]$; sample version $2\hat F(m_1) - 1$. Its sign convention is the opposite of moment skewness, as Asymmetry.
Moors octile kurtosis $\left((E_7 - E_5) + (E_3 - E_1)\right)/(E_6 - E_2)$, $E_k$ the $k$-th octile; sample octiles by R type 7.
The ratio of the mean absolute deviation to the standard deviation, $\mathrm{E}|y-\mu_1|/\sigma$, the order-one analogue of Hypotailedness.

The coefficients built on the half central moment that the study compares with other measures: [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]], [[TM4:Hypotailedness]], [[TM5:Extremity coefficient]] and [[TM8:Complex Extremity]].

The measures the half-moment coefficients are compared with: for skewness, [[TM9:moment skewness]], [[TM11:L-skewness]], [[TM13:TL-skewness]], [[TM15:quartile skewness]], [[TM16:medcouple]] and [[TM17:Tajuddin skewness]]; for tail weight, [[TM10:excess kurtosis]], [[TM12:L-kurtosis]], [[TM14:TL-kurtosis]], [[TM18:octile kurtosis]] and [[TM19:Geary ratio]].

Samples of size $n$ drawn from a base distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$; in each, the first value is replaced by $\mu + k\sigma$. Every measure is computed on the clean sample and on the contaminated one.

For one measure, base distribution, $n$ and $k$: the mean over replications of the measure on the contaminated samples minus its mean on the clean samples, divided by the standard deviation of the measure over the clean samples.
Measurements on 48 rock samples from a petroleum reservoir (BP research), the rock data set of R's datasets package: area, perimeter, shape and permeability.

Daily closing prices of four European stock indices (DAX, SMI, CAC, FTSE), 1991-1998, business days, 1860 observations each: the EuStockMarkets data set of R's datasets package; analysed as daily log returns (1859 each).
Every measure computed on the first $t$ returns of a series, for every $t$ from 30 to the full length.

body.statement: If a variable with a finite mean has a distribution symmetric about its mean, the real and imaginary parts of its [[TM1:half central moment]] are equal.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it.

body.question: Q1

body.statement: Under a change of location the [[TM1:half central moment]] is unchanged; multiplying the variable by $c > 0$ multiplies it by $c^{0.5}$, and multiplying by $c < 0$ multiplies it by $|c|^{0.5}$ and exchanges its real and imaginary parts.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it. The case of a negative factor was added by the agent by reasoning.

about.subject: TM1
about.relation: is invariant to location and scales by the square root of a positive factor

body.statement: For a variable with a finite mean that is not constant, the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] lies in $[-1, 1]$; it is $0$ when the real and imaginary parts of the [[TM1:half central moment]] are equal and negative exactly when the imaginary part, from the values below the mean, is the larger.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it.

about.subject: TM3
about.relation: lies in [-1, 1], with its sign given by the larger part

body.statement: For a variable with a finite mean $\mu_1$ and positive probability on both sides of it, let $p_\pm = P(\pm(y - \mu_1) > 0)$ and $h_\pm = \mathrm{E}\left[|D|^{0.5} \mid \pm D > 0\right] / \left(\mathrm{E}\left[|D| \mid \pm D > 0\right]\right)^{0.5}$ with $D = y - \mu_1$. Then $h_+, h_- \in (0, 1]$, each equal to 1 exactly when the deviations on its side are constant, and the parts of the [[TM1:half central moment]] satisfy $\mathcal{R}(\mu_{0.5})/\mathcal{I}(\mu_{0.5}) = (p_+/p_-)^{0.5}\, h_+/h_-$, so that the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] is determined by the probability on each side of the mean and by how evenly the deviations are spread on each side.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the definitions by reasoning (Jensen's and Lyapunov's inequalities, the mean's balance of deviations); no run informed it.

about.subject: TM3
about.relation: is determined by the probability on each side of the mean and the spread of deviations within each side

body.statement: For a variable with a finite mean $\mu_1$, a finite moment of order 3/2 and positive probability on both sides of $\mu_1$, the mean is the $L_{3/2}$-quantile at level $\tau^* = \mathcal{I}(\mu_{0.5})/\nu_{0.5}$, and the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] equals $\frac{4}{\pi}\arctan(1 - 2\tau^*)$.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Suggested by the literature search of 19 November 2026 (the L_p-quantiles of Chen 1996, doi:10.1016/0167-7152(95)00163-8); no run informed it.

about.subject: TM3
about.relation: is a monotone function of the L_{3/2}-quantile level of the mean

body.statement: For a variable with a finite positive variance, [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] lies in $(0, 1]$ and equals 1 exactly when $|y - \mu_1|$ is constant with probability one; hence the [[TM5:Extremity coefficient]] lies in $(-1, 1]$, is 0 for the uniform distribution and is negative exactly when Hypotailedness is below its uniform value $2 \times 3^{-0.75}$.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it. The case of equality was added by the agent by reasoning.

about.subject: TM4
about.relation: lies in (0, 1], reaching 1 only when the absolute deviation is constant

body.statement: For a sample of $n \geq 2$ values that are not all equal, the sample [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] is at least $2^{0.75} n^{-0.75}$, with equality exactly when two values lie at equal distances on either side of the sample mean and all other values equal it.
body.question: Q1

about.subject: TM4
about.relation: is at least 2^0.75 n^-0.75 in a sample of n values
conditions: a sample of n values not all equal

body.statement: For a variable with a finite positive variance, no probability at its mean and positive probability on both sides of it, each [[TM7:one-sided Hypotailedness]] lies in $(0, 1]$ and equals 1 exactly when the deviations on its side are constant; both equal $2 \times 3^{-0.75}$ for the uniform distribution and both equal [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] for a distribution symmetric about its mean. Hence each part of the [[TM8:Complex Extremity]] lies in $(-1, 1]$ and is 0 for the uniform distribution.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the definitions by reasoning (Jensen's and Lyapunov's inequalities, the mean's balance of deviations); no run informed it.

about.subject: TM8
about.relation: has each part in (-1, 1], 0 for the uniform distribution

body.statement: For the uniform distribution on $(b, c)$, the [[TM1:half central moment]] is $(1+i)\frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{c-b}{2}\right)^{0.5}$, the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] is 0, [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] is $2 \times 3^{-0.75}$ and the [[TM5:Extremity coefficient]] is 0.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it.

body.statement: For the normal distribution with standard deviation $\sigma$, the [[TM1:half central moment]] is $(1+i)\,\Gamma(0.75)\,\pi^{-0.5}\,2^{-0.75}\,\sigma^{0.5}$, the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] is 0 and [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] is $\Gamma(0.75)\,\pi^{-0.5}\,2^{0.25}$.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it.

body.statement: For the Laplace distribution with scale $b$, the [[TM1:half central moment]] is $(1+i)\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4}\,b^{0.5}$ and [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] is $\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\,2^{-0.25}$.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the definitions by reasoning (Jensen's and Lyapunov's inequalities, the mean's balance of deviations); no run informed it.

body.statement: For the generalised normal distribution with shape $s > 0$ and scale $\alpha$ (density proportional to $\exp(-|y/\alpha|^s)$), the [[TM1:half central moment]] is $(1+i)\frac{\alpha^{0.5}}{2}\,\frac{\Gamma(1.5/s)}{\Gamma(1/s)}$ and [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] is $\Gamma(1.5/s)\,\Gamma(1/s)^{-0.75}\,\Gamma(3/s)^{-0.25}$.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the definitions by reasoning (Jensen's and Lyapunov's inequalities, the mean's balance of deviations); no run informed it.

body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it. The condition on the mean was added by the agent.

body.statement: For the Cauchy distribution with location 0 and scale $\gamma$, which has no mean, the [[TM1:half central moment]] taken about its location 0 is $(1+i)\frac{\sqrt{\gamma}}{2}\sec\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: Stated in the manuscript Half Central Moment for Data Analysis (draft of 19 November 2026), written before this record began; no run informed it.

about.relation: has a closed form about its location for

body.statement: For the gamma distribution with shape $a$ and rate $\lambda$ (mean $a/\lambda$), the parts of the [[TM1:half central moment]] are $\mathcal{R}(\mu_{0.5}) = \frac{\Gamma(1.5)\,a^{a+0.5}e^{-a}}{\Gamma(a)\,\lambda^{0.5}}\,U(1.5,\, a+1.5,\, a)$ and $\mathcal{I}(\mu_{0.5}) = \frac{B(a, 1.5)\,a^{a+0.5}}{\Gamma(a)\,\lambda^{0.5}}\,{}_1F_1(a;\, a+1.5;\, -a)$, with $U$ the confluent hypergeometric function of the second kind and ${}_1F_1$ Kummer's function; for $a = 1$ (the exponential distribution) they are $\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2e\sqrt{\lambda}}$ and $\frac{2e - \sqrt{\pi}\,\mathrm{erfi}(1)}{2e\sqrt{\lambda}}$, and the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] does not depend on $\lambda$.
body.question: Q2
body.independence: The exponential case is stated in the manuscript (draft of 19 November 2026); the general gamma form was derived by the agent by reasoning. No run informed either.

body.statement: At a distribution with a finite fourth moment and a density bounded near its mean, the influence function of the [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]] is unbounded and grows linearly in the outlying value $x$ as $|x| \to \infty$, decreasing for large positive $x$; the influence functions of [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] and of the [[TM5:Extremity coefficient]] grow quadratically, through the variance, and decrease in both directions.
body.question: Q1
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the definitions by reasoning (the influence functions of the mean, the partial moments and the variance); no run informed it.

about.subject: TM3
about.relation: has an influence function growing linearly in the outlying value

diagnostics: largest relative error of the numerical checks
body.design: The agent writes a proof of each hypothesis in claimset-code/half-moments/proofs/properties.md. The deciding run (proofs.py properties) copies the proof document into the run and checks each statement numerically: H1, H4, H5, H6, H7, H9 by numerical integration at 40 digits on the normal, uniform, Laplace, Student t(5), exponential, gamma(2), lognormal(0,1) and beta(2,5) distributions; H2 on the three-point distribution of the counterexample; H3 on these distributions and their mirror images, with c = 2, 0.5 and -2; H8 on 10000 random samples for each n in 2, 3, 5, 10, 30 and 100 and on the extremal samples; H17 by the gross-error sensitivity (T((1-e)F + e delta_x) - T(F))/e with e = 1e-6 at x = mu + k sigma, k = 1 to 1000, compared with the derived influence functions. An agent on Claude Fable, registered as its own actor before it starts and working in its own log, then checks every proof step and records one check per hypothesis.
body.analysis: For each hypothesis: the proof, the checker's verdict and the largest relative error of its numerical checks; for H17, the fitted growth exponents of the influence functions over k = 10 to 1000.
body.new_data: H2 and H8 are decided by proofs, which RN1 did not give; their numerical checks use a one-parameter family of asymmetric distributions with equal parts (not only the three-point distribution of RN1) and samples of sizes 2, 30 and 100 with new seeds (RN1 searched n = 3, 5 and 10 only).

decision.not_supported: A counterexample to the statement is found, by the proof attempt, by the checker or by the numerical checks of the run.

body.design: The agent writes the derivation of each closed form in claimset-code/half-moments/proofs/distributions.md. The deciding run (proofs.py distributions) copies the document into the run and evaluates every closed form against numerical integration at 40 digits: uniform (b, c) = (0, 1), (-2, 5); normal sigma = 1, 3; Laplace b = 1, 2.5; generalised normal s = 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 4; Student t nu = 0.75, 1, 1.5, 3, 5, 30; Cauchy gamma = 1, 2; gamma a = 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 20 with lambda = 1, 3. The checker (an agent on Claude Fable, its own actor and log) checks every derivation. Distributions without a closed form (lognormal, beta, Weibull, skew-normal) are listed in a note as needing numerical integration; no values are reported for them.
body.analysis: For each hypothesis: the derivation, the checker's verdict and the largest relative error between the closed form and numerical integration.

body.question: Q3

growth.variable: growth exponent of the standardised shift

diagnostics: Monte Carlo standard error of the standardised shift
body.design: Single-outlier contamination: base distributions normal(0,1), Student t(5) and exponential(1); sample sizes n = 100 and 1000; 10000 replications for each base distribution and n, the same clean samples reused for every k; in each sample the first value replaced by mu + k sigma, k = 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100; seeds fixed (seed 20261120 for the first base distribution and n, incremented for each next one). Every measure of the half-moment coefficients and of the comparison measures is computed on each clean and each contaminated sample.
body.analysis: For each measure, base distribution, n and k: the standardised shift (mean over replications of the measure on contaminated samples minus its mean on clean samples, divided by its standard deviation on clean samples) with its Monte Carlo standard error; and for each measure, base distribution and n, the growth exponent: the slope of log |standardised shift| on log k over k = 10, 20, 50, 100, to set beside the influence functions of H17 (Q1).

choices.choice: an estimate of the response to k, no hypothesis test
normal, t(5), exponential
k = 0.5 to 100 standard deviations from the mean
moment, L-, TL-moment, quartile, medcouple, Tajuddin; excess, L-, TL-, octile kurtosis, Geary ratio
choices.ref: lit search 2026-11-19 (Hosking 1990; Elamir & Seheult 2003; Hinkley 1975; Brys et al. 2004; Tajuddin 1996; Moors 1988; Geary 1935)

body.question: Q4
body.design: The petroleum rock samples (48 samples; area, perimeter, shape, permeability) and the European stock index returns (daily log returns of DAX, SMI, CAC and FTSE, 1859 each). For every variable and index: the half central moment, the half absolute moment, the half-moment coefficients and the comparison measures on the whole sample. For the DAX returns also the expanding window from 30 to 1859 returns.
body.analysis: A table of every measure for every rock variable; a table of every measure for every index; for the DAX expanding window, the first, last, smallest and largest value of each measure, and the window lengths at which each reaches its extremes.

choices.choice: EuStockMarkets daily log returns (public, R datasets) instead of the Bitcoin series
log returns of daily closing prices

body.text: How biased and how variable are the sample half-moment coefficients at realistic sample sizes, what is their limiting distribution, and how well do confidence intervals for them cover?

body.statement: For a variable with a finite fourth moment and a density bounded and continuous near its mean, the sample [[TM3:Asymmetry coefficient]], [[TM4:Hypotailedness]] and [[TM5:Extremity coefficient]] are asymptotically normal: $\sqrt{n}(\hat T_n - T) \to N\left(0, \mathrm{E}\left[\mathrm{IF}_T(y)^2\right]\right)$, where $\mathrm{IF}_T$ is the influence function of the coefficient, which includes the effect of estimating the mean.
body.question: Q5
body.independence: Derived by the agent from the influence functions (H17) and the treatment of statistics with an estimated parameter in Randles (1982, doi:10.1214/aos/1176345787); no run informed it.

about.subject: TM3
about.relation: is asymptotically normal with variance given by its influence function

diagnostics: Monte Carlo standard error of the simulated standard deviation
body.design: The agent writes the proof in claimset-code/half-moments/proofs/asymptotics.md, with the asymptotic variance of each coefficient as E[IF(y)^2] from the influence functions of H17. The deciding run (proofs.py asymptotics) copies the document into the run, computes E[IF(y)^2] by numerical integration for the normal, Student t(5) and exponential distributions, and compares sqrt(E[IF^2]/n) with the standard deviation of each coefficient over 20000 samples of n = 20000 from each (seed 20261121). An agent on Claude Fable, registered as its own actor and working in its own log, checks the proof.
body.analysis: The proof, the checker's verdict, and for each coefficient and distribution the ratio of the simulated standard deviation to the asymptotic one with its Monte Carlo standard error.

choices.choice: an agent on Claude Fable
normal, t(5), exponential, as for the robustness study
within 3 Monte Carlo standard errors; refuted beyond 6

parameters.checker: an agent on Claude Fable (claude-fable-5-2), its own actor and log
parameters.simulation: 20000 samples of n = 20000 per distribution, seed 20261121

decision.supported: A complete proof is in the deciding run's document; the independent checker (an agent on Claude Fable, its own actor and log) confirms it in full with no unresolved dispute; and for every coefficient and distribution the ratio of the simulated to the asymptotic standard deviation is within 3 Monte Carlo standard errors of 1.
decision.not_supported: A counterexample to the statement is found, by the proof attempt or the checker, or for some coefficient and distribution the ratio of the simulated to the asymptotic standard deviation differs from 1 by more than 6 Monte Carlo standard errors.

body.question: Q5
diagnostics: Monte Carlo standard error of the coverage
body.design: Samples from the normal(0,1), Student t(5) and exponential(1) distributions, n = 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000 and 2000; 10000 replications for each distribution and n (seed 20261122, incremented for each next one). On each sample: the sample Asymmetry, Hypotailedness, Extremity and both parts of the Complex Extremity; 95% intervals for each by (a) the normal approximation with a jackknife standard error and (b) the percentile bootstrap with 999 resamples, the bootstrap on the first 2000 replications only. True values from the closed forms of Q2 (normal, exponential) and from numerical integration at 40 digits (t(5)).
body.analysis: For each coefficient, distribution and n: bias (mean minus true value), standard deviation, root mean squared error and sqrt(n) times the standard deviation, each with its Monte Carlo standard error; coverage of the two 95% intervals with its Monte Carlo standard error.

choices.choice: normal, t(5), exponential, as for the robustness study
normal approximation with a jackknife standard error; percentile bootstrap, 999 resamples
10000; bootstrap on 2000
